exercises: Change the verb in brackets to fit the sentence: 어제 도서관에서 (읽다 → ____) 책은 정말 재미있었어요.
Change the verb in brackets to fit the sentence: 내일 면접 때 (입다 → ____) 옷을 미리 골라 놨어요.
Change the verb in brackets to fit the sentence: 공원에서 지금 (놀다 → ____) 아이들이 제 조카들이에요.
Change the adjective in brackets to fit the sentence: 집에서 (가깝다 → ____) 병원이 어디예요?
Change the word in brackets to fit the sentence: 저기 (멋있다 → ____) 모자를 쓴 사람이 우리 선생님이에요.
There are two mistakes in these sentences. Find them and fix them: 오늘은 정말 덥은 날이에요. 그래서 머리가 길은 사람들은 머리를 묶었어요.

forms.when: The action is happening now or happens regularly. Add -는 to the verb stem, whether it ends in a vowel or a consonant: 먹다 → 먹는, 마시다 → 마시는. (Stems ending in ㄹ drop the ㄹ: 살다 → 사는. See the ㄹ-stem row below.)
forms.means: the (noun) that someone does / is doing
forms.example: 지금 커피를 마시는 사람이 제 친구예요.
forms.exampleMeaning: The person who is drinking coffee right now is my friend.

forms.when: The action is already finished. If the stem ends in a consonant, add -은 (먹다 → 먹은). If it ends in a vowel, add -ㄴ (보다 → 본).
forms.exampleMeaning: The food I ate yesterday was a bit salty.

forms.when: The action has not happened yet, or it is something you plan or need to do. If the stem ends in a consonant, add -을 (먹다 → 먹을). If it ends in a vowel, add -ㄹ (보다 → 볼).
forms.means: the (noun) that someone will do / is going to do
forms.example: 이번 주말에 볼 영화를 아직 못 정했어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: I still haven't decided on a movie to watch this weekend.

forms.when: Use this for any adjective describing a noun. If the stem ends in a consonant, add -은 (작다 → 작은). If it ends in a vowel, add -ㄴ (크다 → 큰).
forms.example: 작은 가방 말고 큰 가방 있어요?
forms.exampleMeaning: Do you have a big bag instead of a small one?

forms.when: Words ending in 있다 or 없다 (맛있다, 재미없다, 있다, 없다) take -는 (not -은) to describe a noun in the present, even when they work like adjectives in English.
forms.exampleMeaning: I can't sit through a boring movie.

forms.when: When the stem ends in ㄹ, the ㄹ drops before -는 and -ㄴ. With -ㄹ, the two ㄹ merge into one. Do not add 으. Verbs: 살다 → 사는 / 산 / 살, 만들다 → 만드는 / 만든 / 만들. Adjectives: 길다 → 긴, 멀다 → 먼.
forms.means: same meanings as above (present / past / future, or adjective state)
forms.exampleMeaning: This is a cake I made myself.

forms.when: Most adjectives ending in ㅂ change ㅂ to 우 and then add -ㄴ: 춥다 → 추운, 어렵다 → 어려운. A few are regular and keep ㅂ, for example 좁다 → 좁은.
forms.exampleMeaning: Ask your teacher about difficult words.

objective: Learners will be able to form the correct noun-modifying ending (-는, -(으)ㄴ, -(으)ㄹ) for verbs, adjectives, and irregular stems.
summary: Describing words go before the noun in Korean: verbs take -는 (now), -(으)ㄴ (past), or -(으)ㄹ (future), and adjectives take -(으)ㄴ. 있다/없다 words take -는, ㄹ-stems drop ㄹ, and most ㅂ-adjectives change ㅂ to 우.
title: 명사 꾸미기: -는 / -(으)ㄴ / -(으)ㄹ
watchOut: 맛있은 음식 (X) → 맛있는 음식 (O): Words ending in 있다/없다 take -는 (not -은), even when you are describing a quality.
예쁘는 가방 (X) → 예쁜 가방 (O): Adjectives do not take -는 (except words ending in 있다/없다). They take -(으)ㄴ.
서울에 오래 살은 사람 / 사은 사람 (X) → 서울에 오래 산 사람 (O): With ㄹ-stems, drop the ㄹ and add -ㄴ. Do not add 은. The same goes for 만들은 (X) → 만든 (O).
요즘 매일 먹은 빵 (X) → 요즘 매일 먹는 빵 (O): For a habit that is happening now, use -는. -(으)ㄴ on a verb means the action is finished and in the past.
